text:
The period from 2 to 21 was defined by expansion, internal decay, and fragmentation. The Wougate Crown began by seizing empty land and defeating its rival, the Reswoumark Crown, but ended divided after a succession dispute. Five people held the seat, with an average tenure of 3.8 years and a median of 1.0. The seat passed four times. Two were cast out, one died, one was killed, and one remained at the end.

The Wougate Crown occupied Thu Pits in 2 and declared war on the Reswoumark Crown in 5 for Wei Seam. It defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Wei Seam, killing 29, and took the site. It defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Reswoumark, killing 198, and took that site. The Reswoumark Crown finished in 6. The Wougate Crown made peace in 7. It raided Broldtemoor in 13, carrying off 45 grain and killing 56, and raided Rucrag in 15, carrying off 29 grain and killing 35. It suffered seven raids from House Wem, all beaten off except those in 10 and 11 which carried off plunder.

Hunger lasted 10 years, killing 450. Sus Waernthaeld died in 12. Thris Pou took the seat in 12. Krim Groum challenged Thris Pou in 13, won, and took the seat. Thris Pou was cast out. Deathder Grun challenged Krim Groum in 14, won, and took the seat. Krim Groum was cast out. Naenddaem Houllteind returned from exile in 16. Wei Seam rose in 19. Naenddaem Houllteind’s conspiracy was uncovered in 20, and he was cast out in 21. Thrir Pondsurn had Deathder Grun murdered in 21. Lea Dae contested the claim of Skobas Frul in 21, took the seat, and set aside Skobas Frul’s claim. The Wougate Crown divided: Skobas Frul carried off two places as the Second Crown of Reswoumark.

The period from 42 to 50 was defined by the collapse of the Wougate Crown’s territorial integrity and its subsequent reliance on marital alliances for survival. At the start, the Crown faced a war declared by House Wem over a long-standing grievance. This conflict resulted in two decisive defeats at Wougate, costing 180 and 150 lives respectively, and led to the loss of the settlement of Wougate to House Wem in 43. The Crown’s internal stability was equally fragile, marked by two castings-out for attempted murder. By the end of the period, the Crown had lost its primary seat, suffered three failed raids, and survived only through a series of marriages binding it to House Wem and the Sworn Men of Rucrag.

The initial phase of the period saw the Crown’s authority erode rapidly. In 42, House Wem broke its alliance and declared war, leading to a defeat at Wougate where 180 people died. The following year, House Wem defeated the Crown again at Wougate, killing 150, and took the settlement of Wougate. During this time, Voun Woldlom, who had held the seat since 38, was cast out for an attempted murder on Lea Dae. Drithne Draend took the seat by right of birth in 43. The war lasted two years, ending in peace in 44 after the collapse of the Crown’s position.

Drithne Draend’s rule was short and marked by further internal violence. In 46, he attempted to murder Kurnsa Bealldo, an act that was traced back and resulted in his casting-out. Halweill Tu took the seat by right of birth in the same year. The Crown’s external posture was defensive; its raid on Thu Pits in 45 was beaten off. To secure its position, Drithne Draend married Feald Keim in 46, binding the Crown to House Wem. Halweill Tu married Threihoull Thild in 48, binding the Crown to the Sworn Men of Rucrag.

The final years of the period saw the Crown’s territorial losses solidified and its military efforts consistently repelled. Raids on Wei Seam in 49 and Wougate in 50 were both beaten off. The Crown suffered one raid in 42 by the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Wougate, which carried off 53 grain and killed 27 people. Steaskaes Ve married Bi Binseall in 50, creating another bond with the Sworn Men of Rucrag. Halweill Tu remained holding the seat at the end of the period. The Crown had lost one place, fought two battles and lost both, and endured three failed raids, surviving only through the marriages that tied it to its former enemies and new allies.

The period from year 4 to 7 saw the Reswoumark Crown collapse under the weight of famine and war. It began as a power holding territory at Wei Seam and Reswoumark, but ended as a landless entity with its followers scattered. The decline was driven by a famine at Wei Seam that killed six people and shortened grain supplies, followed by a second wave of famine that killed thirteen more and forced thirty-one to abandon the place. These hardships preceded a declaration of war by the Wougate Crown, which sought control of Wei Seam.

In year 5, the Wougate Crown and its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Wei Seam, killing twenty-nine and taking the site. The conflict continued into year 6, when the Wougate Crown and its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown again at Reswoumark, killing 198 and taking the settlement. During this same year, internal violence marked the end of the ruler Diska Louth, who was killed by Fornhir Threi at Reswoumark. The Reswoumark Crown was finished, becoming landless as its last four followers scattered.

Peace was made in year 7 between the Wougate Crown and the Reswoumark Crown after two years of war, following the collapse of the Reswoumark Crown. The power that had held Wei Seam and Reswoumark was destroyed, its rule ending with the scattering of its remaining supporters.

The period from 22 to 41 saw the Wougate Crown endure a war with House Wem, survive a plague, and lose two places. Seven people held the seat, four cast out, two killed, one still holding at the end. The seat passed six times. The Wougate Crown fought four battles against House Wem, winning two and losing two. It sent three raids, all beaten off. It suffered one raid. It ordered three killings. It lost two places. It endured two years of sickness killing 290. It made three marriages.

In 22, House Wem broke its alliance and declared war. Thrir Pondsurn challenged Lea Dae for the Wougate Crown and won. Thrir Pondsurn took the seat by coup. Lea Dae was cast out. The Wougate Crown defeated House Wem at Thu Pits, 24 dead. In 23, Thrir Pondsurn’s attempt on Tin Kaes failed. Thrir Pondsurn was cast out. The Wougate Crown defeated House Wem at Thu Pits, 20 dead. Tommarn Ri contested the claim of Haepin Maerba. Tommarn Ri took the seat, setting aside Haepin Maerba. Haepin Maerba was cast out. In 24, Tommarn Ri’s attempt on Tin Kaes failed. Tommarn Ri was cast out. House Wem and its allies defeated the Wougate Crown at Thu Pits, 16 dead. House Wem took Thu Pits. Sillmaem Freith took the seat by right of birth.

Sillmaem Freith had Tin Kaes murdered at Broldtemoor in 25. House Wem and its allies defeated the Wougate Crown at Wei Seam, 15 dead. House Wem took Wei Seam. In 26, Sillmaem Freith had Goul Geall murdered at Broldtemoor. House Wem and the Wougate Crown made peace. Kros Ranu’s conspiracy against Sillmaem Freith was uncovered. Kros Ranu was put to death. In 27, Sillmaem Freith had Rein Ga murdered at Broldtemoor. In 28, Pondfern Lull married Koldfaem Trir, binding the Wougate Crown to House Wem. Plague broke out at Wougate, taking 95. In 29, the plague killed 195 and 187 fled. The Wougate Crown’s raid on Thu Pits was beaten off. The Second Crown of Reswoumark and the Wougate Crown swore an alliance.

In 31, Kurnsa Bealldo had Sillmaem Freith murdered at Wougate. Sillmaem Freith was killed. Neildpoun Porn took the seat by right of birth. In 32, Voun Woldlom married Mith Thres, binding the Wougate Crown to the Second Crown of Reswoumark. The Wougate Crown’s raid on Wei Seam was beaten off. In 33, the Wougate Crown’s raid on Broldtemoor was beaten off. In 34, Kurnsa Bealldo’s conspiracy against Neildpoun Porn was uncovered. Kurnsa Bealldo was cast out. In 35, Thraellgul Thalgin challenged Neildpoun Porn openly, won, and took the seat. Neildpoun Porn was killed. In 36, Thraellgul Thalgin married Naerream Thrurei, binding the Wougate Crown to House Wem.

In 38, Thraellgul Thalgin’s attempt on Koldfaem Trir failed. Thraellgul Thalgin was cast out. House Wem raided Wougate, carrying off 33 grain and killing 28. Voun Woldlom took the seat by right of birth. The period ended in 41.

House Wem’s rule over these twenty years was defined by violent succession and shifting alliances. The period began with Sir Tintoull seizing the seat from Kraeth Weageir in 30, a transfer marked by Weageir’s subsequent killing at Broldtemoor. Tintoull’s own rule ended in 35 when he was murdered by Koldfaem Trir, who then took the seat by election. The seat passed again in 39 when Greandoul Krean killed Koldfaem Trir, allowing Lea Dae to assume power. Lea Dae was murdered in 44 by Kurnsa Bealldo, who secured the seat by election and held it until the period’s end. Four rulers held the seat in total, with an average tenure of 3.8 years.

The house engaged in four raids, three of which carried off plunder and one that took nothing. In 36, House Wem raided Reswoumark, taking 59 grain and killing 22. In 38, it raided Wougate, taking 33 grain and killing 28. In 40, it raided Haelabarrow, taking 21 grain and killing 35. In 47, it raided Rucrag, killing 27 but taking nothing. These actions were met with eleven raids against House Wem, all of which were beaten off by the Wougate Crown, the Sworn Men of Rucrag, and the Second Crown of Reswoumark. The house also suffered internal purges, with four of its own people murdered by others within the house.

House Wem’s standing fluctuated, notably falling very low in 34 when Thu Pits rose against it. It fought two wars, spending two years at war. In 42, it declared war on the Wougate Crown, breaking its alliance with them. It defeated the Wougate Crown at Wougate in 42, killing 180, and again in 43, killing 150, before taking Wougate from them. Peace was made in 44 after the collapse of the Wougate Crown. In 48, House Wem declared war on the Sworn Men of Rucrag, defeating them at Rucrag and killing 178. The quarrel between House Wem and the Wougate Crown persisted through two battles.

House Wem’s twenty-year span from 9 to 28 was defined by internal bloodshed and a volatile war with the Wougate Crown. The period began with the house purging its own members, casting out Naenddaem Houllteind for attempted murder and conspiracy, and ending with the ruler Kraeth Weageir holding a seat that had lost all standing. Seven people held the seat in these years, passing from one to another six times. Five were killed, one was cast out, and one remained at the end. The house fought four battles against the Wougate Crown, winning two and losing two, while enduring two years of hunger that killed 197 people at Broldtemoor.

The early years were marked by internal violence and failed external aggression. After Naenddaem Houllteind was cast out and declared an outlaw, House Wem raided Wougate and Haelabarrow, carrying off grain and killing many. The house’s internal stability collapsed when Wealdaern Leasha had Bae Raer murdered, allowing Wealdaern to take the seat by election. Thrirnum Skou then murdered Wealdaern, but was himself executed for conspiracy. Wealdaern returned to the seat, only to be challenged and cast out by Tin Kaes. During this time, the house suffered raids from the Wougate Crown at Broldtemoor and Rucrag, and its own raids on Reswoumark, Wei Seam, Thu Pits, and Wougate were all beaten off.

The conflict with the Wougate Crown escalated into open war in 22. House Wem broke its alliance and declared war, but was defeated at Thu Pits in 22 and 24, losing 24 and 20 men respectively. Rucrag rose against the house in 21, when its standing had fallen very low, and broke away as the Sworn Men of Rucrag. House Wem recovered militarily, defeating the Wougate Crown at Thu Pits in 24 and Wei Seam in 25, taking both places. However, internal purges continued, with Sillmaem Freith killing three successive rulers: Tin Kaes, Goul Geall, and Rein Ga. Wei Seam rose against the house in 27, when its standing had fallen to nothing. The war ended in 26 with peace, but the house had lost two places and endured four years of fighting.

The Sworn Men of Rucrag spent twenty-nine years defined by a cycle of internal instability and external conflict with House Wem. The period began with the break from House Wem in 22, when Difearn Kaerheald took the seat. The power was shaped by the return of eight exiles who filled its ranks, but also by a succession of short, violent rules. Difearn Kaerheald held the seat until 30, when Tommarn Ri won an open challenge. Lea Dae then murdered Tommarn Ri in 35, but Naenddaem Houllteind retained the seat through election. Naenddaem was cast out in 36 after an attempt on Koldfaem Trir failed, and Greandoul Krean took the seat. Greandoul’s rule ended in 48 after an attempt on Kurnsa Bealldo failed, leading to his exile. Threihoull Thild took the seat, was killed by Kurnsa Bealldo in 49, and Skove Pull succeeded him. Skove Pull was also killed by Kurnsa Bealldo in 50, and Bi Binseall took the seat at the end of the period.

The Sworn Men of Rucrag engaged in five raids, four of which were beaten off. A raid on Thu Pits in 33 was beaten off. Raids on Wei Seam and Haelabarrow in 38 were beaten off. A raid on Broldtemoor in 44 was beaten off. Only the raid on Wougate in 42 carried off 53 grain and killed 27. The power suffered one raid on Rucrag in 47 by House Wem, which took nothing. A plague at Rucrag in 37 killed 121 people. Marriages tied the power to House Wem in 26 and the Wougate Crown in 27. Lea Dae courted Bi Binseall away in 34.

The quarrel with House Wem dominated the end of the period. House Wem declared war in 48 and broke its alliance. House Wem defeated the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Rucrag in 48, killing 178. House Wem defeated them again at Rucrag in 49, killing 148. Peace was made in 50 after two years of war. The Sworn Men of Rucrag finished the period with Bi Binseall holding the seat, having lost two battles and endured a plague.

The period from 21 to 51 saw the Second Crown of Reswoumark begin as a breakaway from the Wougate Crown and end in military defeat. Skobas Frul established the new power in 21 by taking two places from the Wougate Crown. The new state survived its early years through an alliance with its former parent in 29, but internal stability was fragile. Skobas Frul died in 30, and Mith Thres took the seat. Mith Thres’s rule was short and violent; he attempted to kill Lea Dae in 40 and was cast out for that act.

Difearn Kaerheald, the named heir, took the seat after Kurnsa Bealldo’s claim was rejected in 40. Difearn Kaerheald held the seat for two years before being killed by Kurnsa Bealldo in 42. The standing of the Second Crown of Reswoumark fell to nothing after this killing, and Haelabarrow rose against it in the same year. Thraellgul Thalgin took the seat by right of birth in 42. His rule ended when he attempted to kill Kurnsa Bealldo in 47 and was cast out.

Voun Woldlom took the seat by right of birth in 47. He held the seat until 51, when he also attempted to kill Kurnsa Bealldo and was cast out. Greandoul Krean took the seat by right of birth in 51. The period ended with the Second Crown of Reswoumark defeated by House Wem at Haelabarrow in 51, with 219 dead. The power had suffered four raids beaten off and three raids suffered, and endured two years of sickness that killed 400 people.

House Wem entered the period as a victor, having defeated the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Rucrag in year 49. The conflict with Rucrag lasted two years before both sides made peace in year 50, exhausted by the fighting. During this time, Kurnsa Bealldo orchestrated the murder of Threihoull Thild at Rucrag in year 49, and later had Skove Pull murdered at the same site in year 50. These acts of violence occurred alongside external threats, as the Wougate Crown’s raid on Wei Seam in year 49 and its raid on Wougate in year 50 were both beaten off.

By year 51, House Wem shifted its focus to the Second Crown of Reswoumark. Citing a long-standing grievance, House Wem declared war on Reswoumark. The campaign concluded at Haelabarrow, where House Wem defeated the Second Crown of Reswoumark, leaving 219 dead. The period ended with House Wem standing as the dominant power in the region, having secured peace with Rucrag and achieved a decisive military victory over Reswoumark.

Kurnsa Bealldo took the seat of House Wem in 44 by election after killing Lea Dae at Broldtemoor. Mith Thres returned from exile to serve the house that same year. In 45, Naerream Thrurei challenged Kurnsa openly for the seat, lost, and was killed by Kurnsa at Broldtemoor. The Sworn Men of Rucrag raided Broldtemoor in 44 and were beaten off. House Wem and the Wougate Crown made peace in 44 after two years of conflict following the collapse of the Wougate Crown.

House Wem extracted 55 silver in tribute from the Sworn Men of Rucrag in 46. Drithne Draend returned from exile to serve in 47. House Wem raided Rucrag in 47, killing 27 but taking nothing. The Wougate Crown publicly slighted House Wem in 48. House Wem declared war on the Sworn Men of Rucrag in 48 over a long-standing grievance, breaking its alliance with them. House Wem defeated the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Rucrag in 48 with 178 dead. Kurnsa had Threihoull Thild murdered at Rucrag in 49. House Wem defeated the Sworn Men of Rucrag at Rucrag in 49 with 148 dead.

The Second Crown of Reswoumark publicly slighted House Wem in 49. House Wem declared war on the Second Crown of Reswoumark in 51 over a long-standing grievance, causing trade to break down. Kurnsa had Skove Pull murdered at Rucrag in 50. House Wem and the Sworn Men of Rucrag made peace in 50 after two years. The Sworn Men of Rucrag publicly slighted House Wem in 51. House Wem defeated the Second Crown of Reswoumark at Haelabarrow in 51 with 219 dead. Kurnsa held the seat until the period ended in 51.

In year 51, House Wem declared war on the Second Crown of Reswoumark over a long-standing grievance, causing trade between the two powers to break down. Within the Crown, Voun Woldlom’s attempt on the life of Kurnsa Bealldo failed and was traced back to him. As a result of this attempted murder, Voun Woldlom was cast out of the Second Crown of Reswoumark.

The war continued with House Wem defeating the Second Crown of Reswoumark at Haelabarrow, where 219 people died. Following the vacancy created by the casting out of Voun Woldlom, Greandoul Krean took the seat of the Second Crown of Reswoumark by right of birth.

The Wougate Crown declared war on the Reswoumark Crown in year 5 over Wei Seam. In that same year, the Wougate Crown and its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Wei Seam, with 29 dead. The Wougate Crown took Wei Seam from the Reswoumark Crown as a result of the defeat.

In year 6, the Wougate Crown and its allies defeated the Reswoumark Crown at Reswoumark, with 198 dead. The Wougate Crown took Reswoumark from the Reswoumark Crown following this victory.

In year 7, the Wougate Crown and the Reswoumark Crown made peace after 2 years of conflict, following the collapse of the Reswoumark Crown.

House Wem declared war on the Wougate Crown in 22, citing a long-standing grievance. The Wougate Crown defeated House Wem at Thu Pits in 22, with 24 dead. The Wougate Crown defeated House Wem at Thu Pits again in 23, with 20 dead.

In 24, House Wem and its allies defeated the Wougate Crown at Thu Pits, with 16 dead. House Wem took Thu Pits from the Wougate Crown in 24. In 25, House Wem and its allies defeated the Wougate Crown at Wei Seam, with 15 dead. House Wem took Wei Seam from the Wougate Crown in 25.

House Wem and the Wougate Crown made peace in 26 after 4 years, both sides exhausted.
